speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happened right before you lost consciousness and how you felt in the moments leading up to the episode?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any warning signs like dizziness, nausea, or visual changes before fainting? REQUEST TEST: ECG

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of similar episodes, and do you experience any chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath during physical exertion? REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the clear trigger of micturition and the rapid recovery, this presentation is classic for a vasovagal syncope. To rule out other causes, do you have a history of diabetes, or do you notice any leg swelling or difficulty breathing when lying flat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episode of loss of consciousness. I also have Regained consciousness quickly without confusion, No urinary incontinence, No bite marks or injuries.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture is very consistent with micturition syncope, a type of reflex syncope. Since the ECG and echocardiogram are normal, I am confident in this diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Micturition Syncope
